symptom: `$Root = import from mapping M.IM($Json)` over an array-rooted JSON structure whose mapping maps the array itself to its root entity (`create M.Root { create M.Item_Root/M.Item = JsonObject {…} }`): mx check 11.14 CE0243 "The mapping used to return a value of type 'List of M.Root', but now returns a value of type 'M.Root'" on the first create — the reporter saw it after re-executing; Studio Pro's "open the action and click OK" cleared it (mendixlabs/mxcli#1734)
cause: types.JsonMappingRootIsList fell back to the JSON structure's root kind whenever the root path did not cross an array, so ANY array-rooted structure read as list-returning — but a root at "(Array)" is the array container itself, one object; only a root at "(Array)|(Object)" (the item, Studio Pro's own shape, #248) yields many
file: mdl/types/mapping_shape.go (JsonMappingRootIsList: a stored root path decides alone); test mdl/types/mapping_shape_test.go
insight: Cardinality is a property of WHERE the mapping roots, not of the structure: the same array-rooted structure gives one object or many depending on whether the root element is the array or its item. A fallback to a coarser source is only safe when the finer one is absent — here the fallback ran whenever the finer source said 'not a list', which turned its 'no' into 'unknown'. The fix is shared by the lint rules (same function). Measured on fresh 11.14.0: base 1 x CE0243 on create; fix 0 on create and after a re-execute with a renamed variable.
